undecided_findings.title: Clearing the instruments tag when the player unmounts strips it from every crash report and blocks it for the rest of the visit
undecided_findings.terms_first: The `instruments` tag = a label on each Sentry report naming the open score's kinds of instrument (`drums,030`, or `sample` for the bundled beat): lap 1's ADD-1, refined in lap 2 by F-24 (three digits), F-25 (`sample`) and F-23 (off while a file opens). ADD-3 = the lap-2 addition, applied without asking to complete the owner's F-25 choice: `clearInstruments()` runs when the player unmounts, so a report from the home page `/` never says `sample`. E901 = the code the error pages show after a React crash; it is sent as an unhandled error, which lowers the health number. Unmount = React removing the player from the page: on a crash, on Back or the wordmark link to `/`, before Try again mounts it again, and twice in development (strict mode).
undecided_findings.whats_wrong: §2.3 says the player sets the tag to `sample` when it mounts, and that `clearInstruments()` removes the tag when it unmounts, after which 'an open still running then changes nothing'. §6 makes that clear permanent: 'after `clearInstruments`, no call changes the tag'. Two things then go wrong, both confirmed by running Next 16.3.6's own error boundary with React 19.2.7. (1) When the player crashes, React runs the player's unmount cleanup (the clear) BEFORE `/play`'s error page runs the effect that sends the E901, so no E901 ever carries the tag; lap 2's residual R32 assumed it did. (2) The clear is a one-way latch for the whole page load. Try again, Back then Play, and the development double mount all mount the player again in the same page load, and the new mount's `tagInstruments('sample')` is ignored, so no report carries the tag for the rest of the visit. §6's own PlayerShell.test.tsx tag cases cannot pass in one file without a test-only reset.
undecided_findings.proposed_fix: Option 1 (recommended): decide by page, not by mount. Remove `clearInstruments()` and its latch; no code calls `Sentry.setTag` for this tag. `beforeSend` calls a new `addInstrumentsTag(event)` that adds the remembered value only to a report sent while the page is `/play` and no open runs. The player sets `sample` each time it mounts. A ref guards the swap's `tagInstruments()`, so an open that outlives its player sets nothing; its `restoreInstruments()` still runs. This changes §1 'Also', the §2.3 function list and 'When the tag changes', §3.3's beforeSend line and §6's two tag cases, and removes the To-verify item about removing a tag with `setTag`. Options 2-4 are in `options`.
undecided_findings.why_it_works: The decision moves from the moment the player unmounts, which React reaches before the error page reports, to the moment a report is sent, when the page is known. Reports from `/` still never carry the tag (ADD-3's goal); the E901 from `/play`'s error page carries the score the crashed player held (R32 becomes true); and every new mount starts from `sample`. The swap guard closes the two stale-open cases the plain page rule misses: 18 of 20 checks become 20 of 20 in the verifier's options matrix.
undecided_findings.drop_consequence: Discard it. Every E901, the unhandled report the health number counts, reaches Sentry with no instruments tag, and after one Back-then-Play, one Try again or the development double mount, no report carries the tag for the rest of the visit.
undecided_findings.basis: React 19.2.7 runs every passive cleanup, a removed child's included, before any new passive effect (react-dom flushPassiveEffects). Next 16.3.6's error boundary replaces the player with the error page and mounts it again on reset. The five tag functions take no token, so report.ts cannot tell a stale open from the current one.

undecided_findings.disposition_hint: DECISION — its own card, with the full comparison (the triage skill's §7: depth per option, the table, a weighted matrix, the decisive trade-off, a recommendation and its flip condition). It changes the mechanism of a settled item (ADD-3, applied without asking in lap 2) and the four reviewers proposed four different fixes, so it is the owner's call, not an auto-resolve. undecided_findings.scenario: You are the owner, reading Sentry. A visitor opens Punk.gp on /play, the header fails while it draws the new title, and /play's error page shows "Error E901" — but the E901 issue's Tags panel has no instruments entry, because the player's unmount removes the tag a moment before the error page sends the report. raw_reviewer_findings.title: Clearing the tag on unmount blocks every later mount
raw_reviewer_findings.why_it_matters: A visitor who leaves /play and comes back in the same page load sends no instruments tag for the rest of the visit, neither `sample` nor an opened score's value. Leaving and returning is client-side here: Back (PlayerHeader.tsx:112-113) or the wordmark link (:144), then Play (app/page.tsx:19); Try again on the player's error page remounts the player too, and reactStrictMode: true (next.config.ts:6) does the same in development. The spec has the player tag `sample` on every mount but makes clearInstruments final, and with the five listed functions report.ts cannot tell a new mount's tagInstruments('sample') from a call by an open that outlived the old player. A PlayerShell.test.tsx that mounts the player more than once will expose this, and resetting report.ts between tests would hide it rather than fix it.
raw_reviewer_findings.suggested_fix: In §2.3, make clearInstruments end only the player that unmounts: it removes the tag, sets the open count to 0 and forgets the remembered value, and the next mount's tagInstruments('sample') applies as on a first visit. Keep 'an open still running then changes nothing' at the call sites: the player and OpenFileControl each keep a mounted ref, and an open whose component has unmounted skips restoreInstruments and the swap's tagInstruments. In §6, replace 'after clearInstruments, no call changes the tag' with 'after clearInstruments the tag is gone and the open count is 0', and add a PlayerShell.test.tsx case: mount, unmount and mount again gives `sample`, and an open left running across the unmount changes nothing.

undecided_findings.title: The token check skips the page files browsers actually download
undecided_findings.terms_first: The token check = `web/scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs`, the build step lap 2 added at the owner's request (ADD-5): it fails the build when the Sentry auth token's value is in a file browsers download. Prerendered page = the HTML and data files `next build` writes for a static page (`/` and `/play` are both static); a browser downloads them when it opens the page. `NEXT_PUBLIC_` = the name prefix that lets Next.js copy an environment variable into browser JavaScript.
undecided_findings.whats_wrong: §4 says the check reads every file under `.next/static`, 'which browsers download', and gives as the reason the token is safe today that 'Next.js copies only `NEXT_PUBLIC_…` variables into the page'. But a static page's HTML and its data payload (`play.html`, `play.rsc`, the `.segments` files) are written under `.next/server/app`, and the 404 and 500 pages are copied to `.next/server/pages`; browsers download all of them. Only browser JavaScript is limited to `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables: a server component such as `web/app/play/page.tsx` can render any variable into the page, or pass it to the client player as a prop. The spike ran the lap-2 draft of the check on a fake build with the token in `.next/server/app/play.html` and `play.rsc`: it passed (exit 0).
undecided_findings.proposed_fix: Option 1 (recommended by both reviewers): walk `.next/static`, `.next/server` and `public/`, the folders browsers download from, and correct §4's premise: only browser JavaScript is limited to `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables, and a server component can render any variable into a prerendered page. Update §1's row and §6's test (a fake `.next/server/app/play.html` that holds the token must fail). Option 2: walk every file under `.next` except `.next/cache`, plus `public/` — no folder list to keep current, but wider than ADD-5's words, and it adds a To-verify item (a real production build must not hold the token in a server-only file).
undecided_findings.why_it_works: The check then reads the files the browser really receives, so the leak the App Router makes easiest — a server value rendered into a static page — fails the build. In the spike both options caught the planted token and named the files, never the value.
undecided_findings.drop_consequence: Discard it. A later change that renders the token into a page ships it to every visitor of /play while the build stays green, and the check gives a false sense of safety.
undecided_findings.basis: Next 16.3.6 writes a static App Router page's `.html`, `.rsc` and `.segments` files under `.next/server/app` (export/worker.js:86, export/routes/app-page.js); `.next/static` holds only the client bundles and assets.

fyi_observations.title: A failed source-map upload still deploys, and the maps are deleted
fyi_observations.suggestion: Option 1 (the reviewer): pass `errorHandler: (error) => { throw error; }` to `withSentryConfig`, so a failed release or upload step stops the production build; Vercel keeps the previous deployment, and a redeploy retries. fyi_observations.tradeoff: Deploy availability against readable stack traces: under option 1, while Sentry is down or the token is revoked, no production deploy succeeds (removing SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN from Vercel lets one through without maps); under option 2 a release's traces can be unreadable and only one build-log line says so.

fyi_observations.recommended: Approve option 1 — it fails loudly, like the repository's other build checks; flip to option 2 if a Sentry outage must never block a production deploy. The evidence confirms the facts but does not decide the trade-off, so give it its own question, not a checkbox.
fyi_observations.scenario: You revoke the Sentry token by mistake, then merge a pull request. Vercel's production build logs one line, "An error occurred. With the throwing `errorHandler`, the same deploy fails on Vercel instead, the previous deployment stays live, and the failed deploy tells you to fix the token.

residual_concerns: R40 (feasibility, product-lens, adversarial): Sentry caps a tag value at 200 characters, and the `instruments` value grows by 4 characters per distinct program, so a score with about 49 or more distinct General MIDI programs loses its tag. Rare (a large orchestral MusicXML file); lap 2's F-24 spike measured every fixture well under the limit.

R41 (security-lens): the token check matches the raw value only, so a base64- or URL-encoded copy would pass. Each page's `.rsc` file holds the payload whole, so walking `.next/server` (F-32) also covers the chunked copy inside the HTML.

R42 (adversarial, product-lens): Release Health counts every page load (Sentry 11's "page" session lifecycle; lap 1's Q3 asked the plan to read it), including visits that never leave `/`. The health share therefore moves when more or fewer visitors press Play: 60 home-only visits plus 40 player visits with 20 E202s read 80%. S4 is settled; a measurement note.

R43 (adversarial): an engine import that never settles leaves the loading skeleton forever and sends nothing: E204's clock starts only once the engine exists, and E201 needs a rejection. Predates the spec.

R44 (adversarial): Firefox storage failures that come from the visitor's own profile but are not refusals (NS_ERROR_FILE_CORRUPTED, UnknownError) fall into S2b's 'anything else: error' branch and send one error per page load for that visitor.

R45 (adversarial): storage is read during render (useRestoredTransport's render-phase adjustment, PlayerShell's useState initializer), so S2b's breadcrumb is recorded during render — twice under development's strict mode; harmless in production.

R46 (product-lens): if `beforeSend` throws, Sentry 11 drops the event (`callback_error`) and never updates the session, so a bug in `scrubEvent` or `isKnownEngineNoise` on an unusual event shape removes that whole class of reports and keeps those visits out of the unhandled count. The spec does not say which goal wins when the privacy filter itself fails. Sits beside R9 and R19.

R47 (product-lens): setup step 6 runs in the owner's own browser, where an ad blocker can block Sentry's ingest host just as D3 accepts for visitors; the E103 then never arrives and the setup looks broken. Step 6 could say: use a browser with no ad blocker.

R48 (product-lens): the calls that take the `instruments` tag off and put it back live in the two open paths (pick and drop), not in `requestNotation`. A third open path, such as the paused catalog's 'find a piece to play', would send its failures with the previous song's instruments, and no test or lint rule would notice. Paused work.

R49 (coherence): §3.3 removes the default `Breadcrumbs` integration and adds `breadcrumbsIntegration({ dom: false })` back on the next line; correct, but it can be misread at first as removing breadcrumbs.

decided_findings.type_check: Run in the triage half with TypeScript 5.9.3 against @sentry/nextjs 11.0.0's published types: `Integration` is NOT exported from `@sentry/nextjs` (its types entry merges client, server and edge with `export *`), so the spec names no Integration type. `Event`, `ErrorEvent` and `EventHint` are exported. `addInstrumentsTag(event: SentryEvent): void` (import type { Event as SentryEvent }) and the inline `{ name: 'InstrumentsTag', preprocessEvent: addInstrumentsTag }` in the `integrations` callback compile (exit 0); a negative control with a wrong hook signature fails (exit 2). A type derived from `breadcrumbsIntegration` does not work: its `name` is the literal 'Breadcrumbs'.
decided_findings.research_other_apps: Sentry's docs present beforeSend for filtering and scrubbing, run last after every event processor; event processors and integrations are where they add data. GitHub code search (rough counts): for a tag on every report, `Sentry.setTag` updated when state changes (~75 files) and adding the tag in beforeSend (~70) are about equally common; larger apps (Lightdash, Expensify, WorkAdventure) lean on setTag; Plasmic adds its open project's id in beforeSend at send time; integrations or processors that add tags are rare in app code (PostHog's Sentry integration is one); none of 66 files that mention onRouterTransitionStart with setTag sets a tag in that hook.
